{"caption":"A three-part workflow diagram showing how an agent explores an environment, learns from experience, and assigns credit to improve its policy.","description":"The diagram has three large left-to-right stages beneath a shared workflow. Across the top, an Environment icon leads right to Self-Questioning, then a Task icon leads right to Self-Navigating, then a Trajectory icon leads right to Self-Attributing, and finally a Policy rocket. The stage labels and arrows indicate the sequence from environment and task generation, through trajectory learning, to policy improvement. Orange-bordered artifact boxes and orange arrows mark downward flows within each stage.

In Self-Questioning, the Environment Exploration panel shows Available Tools as small tool icons and an Environment Profile as a collection of environment-related icons. Below, a branching path of gray nodes is labeled Curiosity-Driven Exploration; a blue dashed curved arrow indicates the exploration path leading toward an Exploration Trajectory box. The orange vertical flow is Env. → Exploration Trajectory → Task Draft → Task. The Task Synthesis panel takes an Exploration Trajectory and User Pref. (difficulty and style, illustrated with bars and style icons); an arrow labeled Summarize leads to a Task containing Query, Reference Trajectory, and Task items. In Task Curation, reference trajectories are replayed: the Replay Successfully path is green and has a check mark, while the Fail path is marked Unreachable and has a red crossed marker and a gray circled cross. These outcomes feed a Feasible Task box, which contains query, reference-trajectory, and task icons and is marked with a green check.

In Self-Navigating, Experience Acquisition shows Historical Trials connected by an arrow labeled Construct to an Experience Pool. A dashed connection labeled Retrieve links the pool toward the task/experience area. The orange flow is Task → Experience → Trajectory → Enhance. Experience-mixed Rollout compares Experience-guided paths with Experience-free paths. The guided section has three colored node trajectories labeled w/ Exp 1, w/ Exp 2, and w/ Exp 3; each has a green circled check, and a small adjacent list shows Exp 1, Exp 2, and Exp 3. The experience-free section has two gray node trajectories labeled w/o Exp, each marked with a gray circled cross. In Experience Incorporation, Trajectories w/ exp masked feed an Optimize step, which leads to a small rising-bar graphic labeled P(trajectory | task); an enhancement/agent icon labels the output as Enhance.

In Self-Attributing, Step-level Attribution receives Task, Trajectory, and Reward inputs, shown as three stacked boxes with arrows into an LLM icon. The LLM output associates trajectory steps with three green GOOD labels and one red BAD label along a sequence of nodes. The orange flow is Trajectory → Attribution → Combined Reward → Policy. In Attribution Outcome Integration, an Attribution box shows GOOD and BAD signals with +1 and −1 values and a normalization label; an Outcome Reward box shows a trophy and its own normalization label. Arrows combine these into a Combined Reward expression. In Advantage Computation, step-level advantages A1–A4 are shown above a triangular accumulation of combined-reward terms, with the formula A_t = a sum of reward terms from step t onward. A downward arrow labeled Broadcast to Token-level Advantage leads to the policy output. Green GOOD/check marks indicate favorable steps or outcomes; red BAD/cross marks indicate unfavorable ones. The small environment, clipboard, route, trophy, and rocket icons denote the environment, tasks, trajectories, rewards, and policy in this workflow.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
